## 1. What was read

**832 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **277** records (25% of the 1,109 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 483 | 192 | 88 | 314 | 32 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: sysbio +33%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). This month is missing *Nat Mach Intell*. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nucleic Acids Res 125, JAMA 112, Nature 106, Science 83, Bioinformatics 60, Lancet 50.

## 3. The evidence that moved it











**The Virtual Cell Challenge is launched**
([40578317](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40578317/), *Cell*, 26 June) — framed
in its own title as a Turing test for the virtual cell. Every dating claim this
corpus makes about virtual-cell vocabulary should be measured from here, and note
that the phrase was already in a *Nature Biotechnology* title two months earlier.

**In the same month, the refutation of the thing being launched.**
[40407144](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40407144/) (*Bioinformatics*, 2 June):
**simple controls exceed the best deep learning algorithms for predicting genetic
perturbations.** Perturbation prediction is the challenge's central task. The
corpus later treats "simple baselines match deep models" as a 2026 phenomenon and
reads the July 2026 scaling nulls as the moment the premise broke; the claim was
in print, in a title, three weeks before the challenge that assumed otherwise.
[40434923](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40434923/) says the same thing for
variant effects in the same month: conservation and solvent accessibility are
almost all you need.

**An autonomous agent is validated for clinical decisions.**
[40481323](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40481323/) (*Nat Cancer*): development
and validation of an autonomous AI agent for clinical decision-making in
oncology. This paragraph used to date the arrival by counting months forward from
a February origin; `data/threads.yml` has voided that origin, and an agent is
already the subject of a *Nature Cancer* piece in
[2024-12](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39690222/) in any case. No interval
replaces it. What the card is worth is what it contains — an agent with a
validation study behind it, in an oncology journal — not its position in a chain.

**The checkpoint roster turns over completely.** June nominates Siglec-G/10,
CMTM4, STS2, Piezo1, TTLL12, plus PSGL-1 as a phagocytosis checkpoint, TIM-3 and
ENT1 — eight targets, **all preclinical, none with an agent**. Of May's five, one
reappears. The templated block is at 31, near its peak. A field can be
simultaneously at maximum output and producing nothing that will be tested.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[40457060](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40457060/): PD-1 receptor deficiency
*enhances* CD30+ Treg function in melanoma — removing the checkpoint strengthens
the suppressive population, which is the mechanism by which anti-PD-1 could make
a subset of patients worse.

[40482640](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40482640/) (*Cell*): microbiome
mismatches from microbiota transplants produce persistent off-target metabolic
and immunomodulatory effects. Filed against the neuro-immune-microbiome thread,
and directly relevant to the faecal-transplant trials the thread later counts as
supports.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    Three more cards were listed here as refutations. None of them is one, and
    two of them were misread the same way — from the cell type named in the
    title rather than from the outcome reported in the abstract.

    [40202509](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40202509/), "MYO1F in neutrophils
    is required for the response to immune checkpoint blockade", was taken as a
    suppressive population being necessary for immunotherapy. The paper says
    tumour-associated neutrophils are a significant barrier, that MYO1F is what
    restrains their suppression, and that tumour-derived TGF-beta1 silencing it
    is what drives them into a STAT3-dependent immunosuppressive state that
    exhausts CTLs.

    [40146036](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40146036/) was taken as an
    inversion because a dendritic cell — presenting and stimulatory by
    convention — is the suppressor. Its outcome is the thread's claim verbatim:
    "moDC depletion limits Treg generation and improves the therapeutic outcome
    of RT". A newly identified suppressive population whose depletion helps
    supports the claim; only the identity of the population is new.

    [40335697](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40335697/) (*Nature*, oncogene
    aberrations drive medulloblastoma progression, not initiation) was read from
    its title as bad news for interception. What it does is re-time the driver
    events: the initiating lesions in group 3/4 medulloblastoma are large-scale
    chromosomal aberrations dated to the first gestational trimester, with
    single-gene oncogene hits arriving late and mostly subclonal. Its own
    conclusion is that single-cell technologies "can be applied for early
    detection and diagnosis of this fatal disease". It neither treats a precursor
    state nor shows interception failing, so it now sits on neither side of the
    ratio.

### (b) Method credibility

[40163891](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40163891/) (*Blood*): hallmarks of
T-cell exhaustion and antigen experience are **absent** in multiple myeloma from
diagnosis through maintenance. A negative result against a framework, published
in the disease where the framework is most heavily invoked.

[40578363](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40578363/) (*Immunity*): diet-derived
LPS determines intestinal IgA induction and repertoire **independently of the
microbiota**. It reassigns to diet what a large literature credits to microbes,
which makes it both a method-credibility card and a warning about the
microbiome arm of the neuro-immune thread.

[40240607](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40240607/) (*Nature*): low overlap
between transcription factor DNA binding and regulatory targets.

[40195448](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40195448/) (*Nat Med*): sociodemographic
biases in medical decision making by large language models — title-stated
empirical evidence of failure, in a month whose clinical-AI counterweight is
otherwise governance commentary.
